title: Domain security
notChecked: Not checked yet. The first check reads public DNS, registration and the website, and takes a few seconds.
summary: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing to fix} one {# problem to fix} other {# problems to fix}}

where.dns: Add it at your DNS host
where.dnssec: Switch it on at your DNS host
where.registrar: Only your registrar can do this

passed: {count, plural, one {# check passed} other {# checks passed}}

fix.title: Fixes for {domain}
fix.intro: Nothing changes until you apply. A record already published is shown next to what replaces it.
fix.none: Polaris has nothing to change here. What is left is fixed at your registrar or on your server.
fix.dnssecHint: Your registrar then needs the DS record the zone shows. A domain registered with Cloudflare gets it on its own.
fix.edgeHint: HSTS for 6 months, no MIME sniffing, a strict referrer policy and framing by the same site only, on {hostname}.

policy.label: DMARC policy
policy.hint: Tighten only once every service that sends as {domain} passes - the senders list shows which do. Failing mail then goes to spam (quarantine) or is refused (reject).

fix.applied: {ok, plural, one {# change made} other {# changes made}}
fix.someFailed: {failed, plural, one {# change was not made} other {# changes were not made}}: {detail}
fix.cannotOwner: Polaris publishes these for you once this domain has a Cloudflare token (under its certificate).
fix.cannotAdmin: Polaris publishes these for you when the Cloudflare account connected under Integrations holds this zone.

dedicated.label: Keep it fixed automatically
dedicated.hint: For a domain only Polaris uses. The daily check publishes the safe fixes itself - never a stricter DMARC policy - and tells you what it changed.
dedicated.last: {applied, plural, one {Last automatic fix: # change,} other {Last automatic fix: # changes,}}

reports.title: Who sends as {domain}
reports.intro: From the DMARC reports receivers sent in the last 30 days, worst first.

hints.authorized: All its mail passed. If you do not recognize this sender, an account or key that sends as the domain is compromised.
hints.misconfigured: Some mail failed but it signs or passes SPF for some domain: a real sender that needs adding to SPF or signing with DKIM.
hints.spoofing: Every message failed and nothing signed it: somebody forging the domain. DMARC at reject refuses this mail.

reports.noneYet: No reports yet. Receivers send them once a day to {address}.
reports.elsewhere: Reports for {domain} go to {hosts}, so they are read there, not in Polaris. Polaris reads them for domains on its own mail server.
reports.nowhere: No report address is published, so nobody learns who sends as {domain}. Polaris reads reports for domains on its own mail server.

admin.intro: Every domain Polaris knows, checked each day for spoofing, DNS, registration and HTTPS problems. You are told when one gets worse.
admin.empty: Polaris does not know any domain yet. Set one up above, connect a Cloudflare account, or deploy on a domain of your own.
admin.problems: {count, plural, =0 {No problems} one {# problem} other {# problems}}

errors.notFound: That domain is not one you can see here.
errors.cannotFix: Polaris cannot write this domain's DNS.
errors.planChanged: The records changed since the preview. Review the fixes again.
errors.tooSoon: It was checked a moment ago.
errors.failed: That did not work. Try again in a moment.

notice.worse: {domain}: {count, plural, one {# new security problem} other {# new security problems}}
notice.worseBody: {fixed, plural, =0 {Open the domain to see what to fix.} one {Polaris fixed # record itself. Open the domain to see what is left.} other {Polaris fixed # records itself. Open the domain to see what is left.}}
notice.fixed: {domain}: Polaris fixed {count, plural, one {# record} other {# records}}
notice.fixedBody: The daily check found problems it could fix itself and published the fixes.

mxOk.title: Mail servers published
mxOk.risk: Mail for the domain goes to {hosts}.

mxNull.title: Declares it takes no mail
mxNull.risk: A null MX tells senders not to try, so nothing waits in a queue for it.

mxMissing.title: No mail servers
mxMissing.risk: The domain sends mail but has no MX, so replies and bounces cannot come back and some receivers refuse its mail.
mxMissing.fix: Publish the MX of the service that takes its mail, or the null MX below if nobody should write to it.

spfOk.title: SPF is valid
spfOk.risk: It ends in {all} and costs {lookups} of the 10 DNS lookups allowed.

spfMissing.title: No SPF record
spfMissing.risk: Anybody can send mail claiming to be from this domain, and nothing tells receivers it is forged.
spfMissing.fix: {parked, select, yes {This domain sends no mail: publish an SPF that allows nobody.} other {Publish one SPF listing every service that sends as the domain. The record below is a start; add each provider's include.}}

spfMultiple.title: More than one SPF record
spfMultiple.risk: With {count} SPF records receivers stop at an error and treat every message as unauthenticated.
spfMultiple.fix: Merge them into one record. Polaris merges them for you when it manages the zone.

spfSyntax.title: SPF does not parse
spfSyntax.risk: Receivers stop at "{term}" and treat every message as unauthenticated.

spfAllPass.title: SPF allows everybody
spfAllPass.risk: +all authorizes every server on the internet to send as the domain, which is worse than no SPF.

spfAllNeutral.title: SPF ends in ?all
spfAllNeutral.risk: ?all treats unlisted servers as neutral, so forged mail is not marked.
spfAllNeutral.fix: End the record with ~all, or -all once every sender is listed.

spfAllSoft.title: SPF ends in ~all
spfAllSoft.risk: Unlisted servers soft-fail: forged mail is marked but not refused. With DMARC at reject this is enough.
spfAllSoft.fix: Move to -all once every sender is listed, or rely on DMARC enforcement.

spfAllMissing.title: SPF has no all term
spfAllMissing.risk: Without an all term unlisted servers are neutral, and forged mail passes unmarked.

spfLookups.title: SPF needs too many lookups
spfLookups.risk: It needs {count} DNS lookups. Past 10, receivers stop with an error and SPF fails for all mail.
spfLookups.fix: Remove includes you no longer use, or replace them with the ip4 and ip6 ranges they list.

spfVoid.title: SPF points at missing names
spfVoid.risk: {count} lookups found nothing. Past 2, receivers stop with an error.
spfVoid.fix: Remove the includes and mechanisms that point at names that are gone.

spfIncludeMissing.title: SPF include has no SPF
spfIncludeMissing.risk: {target} publishes no valid SPF, so checking ends with a permanent error.
spfIncludeMissing.fix: Remove the include, or correct it to the provider's current name.

spfPtr.title: SPF uses ptr
spfPtr.risk: The ptr mechanism is slow, unreliable and deprecated; some receivers skip it.
spfPtr.fix: Replace it with ip4, ip6 or include terms.

spfUnchecked.title: SPF could not be checked
spfUnchecked.risk: The public resolvers did not answer. It is tried again on the next check.

dkimNone.title: No DKIM key found
dkimNone.risk: None of the common selectors ({selectors}) has a key. Without DKIM, forwarded mail loses its SPF pass and fails DMARC.
dkimNone.fix: Turn on DKIM signing at each service that sends as the domain and publish the key it gives you. If yours uses another selector, ignore this.

dkimWeak.title: Weak DKIM key
dkimWeak.risk: Selector {selector} uses a {bits}-bit key, which can be broken and is refused by large receivers.
dkimWeak.fix: Generate a 2048-bit key at the sending service and publish it.

dkimShort.title: DKIM key is 1024-bit
dkimShort.risk: Selector {selector} uses {bits} bits. It works, but 2048 is the current recommendation.
dkimShort.fix: Rotate to a 2048-bit key at the sending service.

dkimTesting.title: DKIM key in test mode
dkimTesting.risk: Selector {selector} has t=y, so receivers may ignore failed signatures.

dmarcOk.title: DMARC is enforced
dmarcOk.risk: Policy {policy}, subdomains {sp}. Forged mail is refused or sent to spam.

dmarcMissing.title: No DMARC policy
dmarcMissing.risk: Receivers have no instruction for mail that fails SPF and DKIM, so forged mail claiming this domain is delivered.
dmarcMissing.fix: {parked, select, yes {This domain sends no mail: publish a policy that rejects everything.} other {Start at p=none to collect reports, then move to quarantine and reject once every sender passes.}}

dmarcMultiple.title: More than one DMARC record
dmarcMultiple.risk: With {count} records receivers ignore DMARC entirely.

dmarcSyntax.title: DMARC does not parse
dmarcSyntax.risk: Receivers cannot read "{term}" and ignore the policy.
dmarcSyntax.fix: Correct the record: it starts with v=DMARC1 followed by p=.

dmarcNone.title: DMARC only monitors
dmarcNone.risk: With p=none forged mail is still delivered; it only asks for reports.
dmarcNone.fix: Once every sender passes, move to quarantine, then reject.

dmarcQuarantine.title: DMARC quarantines
dmarcQuarantine.risk: Forged mail goes to spam rather than being refused.
dmarcQuarantine.fix: Move to reject once nothing legitimate is quarantined.

dmarcPct.title: DMARC covers part of the mail
dmarcPct.risk: pct={pct} applies the policy to {pct}% of failing mail; the rest is delivered.
dmarcPct.fix: Raise pct to 100, or remove it.

dmarcSubdomainWeaker.title: Subdomains less protected
dmarcSubdomainWeaker.risk: sp={sp} is weaker than p={p}, so mail forged from a subdomain gets through more easily.
dmarcSubdomainWeaker.fix: Set sp to {p}, or remove it so subdomains inherit the policy.

dmarcRuaMissing.title: No DMARC reports requested
dmarcRuaMissing.risk: Without rua nobody learns who sends as the domain, so spoofing and broken senders go unseen.
dmarcRuaMissing.fix: Add rua=mailto: with an address that receives reports.

dmarcRuaUnauthorized.title: Report address not authorized
dmarcRuaUnauthorized.risk: {host} has not published that it accepts reports for this domain, so receivers drop them.
dmarcRuaUnauthorized.fix: Publish the authorization record at {host}, or use an address on this domain.

parkedOk.title: Locked down, sends no mail
parkedOk.risk: SPF allows nobody, DMARC rejects and the null MX refuses mail: the domain cannot be used for spoofing.

parkedNullMx.title: No null MX
parkedNullMx.risk: The domain sends and takes no mail. A null MX says so, and senders stop retrying.

parkedDkim.title: No empty DKIM key
parkedDkim.risk: An empty wildcard key makes any DKIM signature claiming this domain fail at once.

mtaStsOk.title: MTA-STS enforced
mtaStsOk.risk: Senders must deliver over verified TLS to the listed servers.

mtaStsMissing.title: No MTA-STS
mtaStsMissing.risk: Senders may fall back to unencrypted delivery if an attacker strips TLS on the way.
mtaStsMissing.fix: Serve a policy file on the mta-sts subdomain and publish its _mta-sts TXT record.

mtaStsPolicy.title: MTA-STS policy not served
mtaStsPolicy.risk: The TXT record exists but {host} serves no valid policy, so senders cannot use it.
mtaStsPolicy.fix: Serve a valid policy at https://{host}/.well-known/mta-sts.txt.

mtaStsTesting.title: MTA-STS not enforced
mtaStsTesting.risk: The policy is in {mode} mode: failures are reported, not prevented.
mtaStsTesting.fix: Switch the mode to enforce once reports show no failures.

mtaStsMxMismatch.title: MTA-STS misses an MX
mtaStsMxMismatch.risk: The policy enforces TLS but does not list {hosts}, so senders refuse to deliver there.
mtaStsMxMismatch.fix: Add those hosts to the policy's mx lines.

tlsRptOk.title: TLS reporting on
tlsRptOk.risk: Senders report deliveries that failed over TLS.

tlsRptMissing.title: No TLS reporting
tlsRptMissing.risk: Nobody hears when senders fail to deliver over TLS.
tlsRptMissing.fix: Publish a TLS-RPT record with an address that receives reports.

bimiOk.title: BIMI published
bimiOk.risk: Inboxes that support it can show the brand logo.

bimiIneligible.title: BIMI not in effect
bimiIneligible.risk: BIMI needs DMARC at quarantine or reject with pct=100, so the logo is not shown.

dnssecOk.title: DNSSEC signed and valid
dnssecOk.risk: Resolvers can verify that answers really come from the zone.

dnssecOff.title: DNSSEC off
dnssecOff.risk: Answers for the domain can be forged on the way to a resolver (cache poisoning).
dnssecOff.fix: Sign the zone at the DNS host, then add the DS record it gives you at the registrar.

dnssecNoDs.title: Signed, no DS at registrar
dnssecNoDs.risk: The zone is signed but its parent does not vouch for it, so nobody validates it.
dnssecNoDs.fix: Add the zone's DS record at your registrar.

dnssecBroken.title: DNSSEC fails validation
dnssecBroken.risk: The DS at the registrar does not match the zone's keys, so validating resolvers do not answer at all.
dnssecBroken.fix: Replace the DS at the registrar with the one your DNS host shows, or remove it.

caaOk.title: CAA restricts certificates
caaOk.risk: Only {issuers} may issue certificates for the domain.

caaMissing.title: No CAA record
caaMissing.risk: Any certificate authority may issue certificates for the domain.
caaMissing.fix: Publish CAA records naming the authorities you use. Polaris uses Let's Encrypt.

caaBlocksPolaris.title: CAA blocks Polaris
caaBlocksPolaris.risk: CAA allows {issuers} but not Let's Encrypt, so certificates Polaris orders here fail.
caaBlocksPolaris.fix: Add the record below alongside the existing ones.

nsOk.title: Name servers redundant
nsOk.risk: {count} name servers on more than one network.

nsSingle.title: Only one name server
nsSingle.risk: {count} found. If it goes down the domain stops resolving.
nsSingle.fix: Use at least two name servers; your DNS host lists them.

nsSameNetwork.title: Name servers on one network
nsSameNetwork.risk: Every name server is in {block}, so one outage takes them all down.
nsSameNetwork.fix: Add a name server on another network.

axfrRefused.title: Zone transfers refused
axfrRefused.risk: {count, plural, one {The name server refuses} other {All # name servers refuse}} to hand out the whole zone.

axfrOpen.title: Zone transfer allowed
axfrOpen.risk: {server} hands the whole zone to anybody, listing every hostname you have.
axfrOpen.fix: Restrict zone transfers on that server to your secondaries.

danglingOk.title: No dangling aliases
danglingOk.risk: {count, plural, one {# alias checked} other {# aliases checked}}; all point at names that exist.

danglingCname.title: Alias to a name that is gone
danglingCname.risk: {name} points at {target}, which no longer exists. Whoever registers it can serve content on your name.
danglingCname.fix: Remove the record, or point it at a name you control.

wildcard.title: Wildcard record
wildcard.risk: {name} answers for every name, which makes a forgotten subdomain look live.
wildcard.fix: Keep it only if a service needs every name. Polaris's own zones use one on purpose.

rdapUnavailable.title: Registration not checked
rdapUnavailable.risk: The registry publishes no RDAP for this name, so expiry and locks could not be read.

expirySoon.title: Expires on {date}
expirySoon.risk: In {days} days. A lapsed domain stops resolving and anybody can register it.
expirySoon.fix: Renew it at your registrar and turn on auto-renew.

transferLocked.title: Transfer lock on
transferLocked.risk: The registrar refuses transfers until the lock is lifted.

transferUnlocked.title: No transfer lock
transferUnlocked.risk: Anybody who gets into the registrar account, or the mailbox behind it, can move the domain away.
transferUnlocked.fix: Turn on the transfer lock (clientTransferProhibited) at your registrar.

registrantPrivate.title: Registrant details private
registrantPrivate.risk: RDAP does not publish who holds the domain.

registrantPublic.title: Registrant details public
registrantPublic.risk: RDAP shows who holds the domain, which phishers and spammers use.
registrantPublic.fix: Turn on privacy (redaction) at your registrar.

webNone.title: No website
webNone.risk: The domain has no address, so there is no site to check.

httpsUnreachable.title: No HTTPS
httpsUnreachable.fix: Serve the site over HTTPS. Polaris issues certificates for the services it deploys.

certInvalid.title: Certificate not trusted
certInvalid.fix: Install a certificate for this name from a trusted authority.

certExpiring.title: Certificate expires {date}
certExpiring.risk: In {days} days. After that browsers block the site.
certExpiring.fix: Renew it, or find out why automatic renewal stopped.

tlsLegacy.title: Old TLS accepted
tlsLegacy.risk: The server still accepts {version}, which is deprecated and weak.

httpRedirectMissing.title: HTTP not redirected
httpRedirectMissing.risk: Visitors who type the name land on unencrypted HTTP.

hstsOk.title: HSTS on
hstsOk.risk: Browsers use HTTPS only, for {maxAge} seconds.

hstsMissing.title: No HSTS
hstsMissing.risk: A visitor's first request can be downgraded to HTTP and intercepted.
hstsMissing.fix: Send Strict-Transport-Security with a max-age of at least 6 months.

hstsShort.title: HSTS too short
hstsShort.risk: max-age={maxAge} lapses quickly, so the protection does not hold between visits.
hstsShort.fix: Raise max-age to at least 15552000 (6 months).

headersOk.title: Security headers present
headersOk.risk: Framing, MIME sniffing and referrer leaks are restricted.

headerFramingMissing.title: Can be framed by other sites
headerFramingMissing.risk: Without frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options another site can embed the page and trick clicks (clickjacking).

headerNosniffMissing.title: MIME sniffing allowed
headerNosniffMissing.risk: Without X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff a browser may run an upload as a script.

headerReferrerMissing.title: No referrer policy
headerReferrerMissing.risk: Full addresses, query strings included, leak to every site you link to.

headerCspMissing.title: No Content Security Policy
headerCspMissing.risk: Nothing limits where scripts load from, so an injected script runs freely.
headerCspMissing.fix: Add a policy that fits the site. A generic one breaks most apps, so Polaris does not set it on its own.

securityTxtOk.title: security.txt published
securityTxtOk.risk: Researchers know where to report a vulnerability.

securityTxtMissing.title: No security.txt
securityTxtMissing.risk: Whoever finds a vulnerability has no published contact.
securityTxtMissing.fix: Publish {url} with a Contact and an Expires line.

securityTxtExpired.title: security.txt expired
securityTxtExpired.risk: Its Expires date ({date}) has passed, so reporters may treat the contact as stale.
